messages:
nate: Heads-up - multiple customers in EU reporting mTLS failures this morning. Error is client TLS handshake failing with 'bad certificate' and when I ran an s_client I got the default edge cert instead of the customer cert. :confused:

jordan: Which LB/ingress fronting the vhost? ALB or NLB? Any recent listener changes?

nate: ALB (TLS listener) -> target group -> kube ingress (nginx) doing mTLS. No recent ingress deploys, did push a few ALB certs last night (rotations).

cami: Pasted ALB access logs: 2026-03-18T06:12:34Z alb-1 10.0.0.1:443 10.0.1.45:61023 "GET /health 200" "app-cust.example.com" tg/primary 0.002 0.003 0.005 200 200 0 "-" "-"
Looks like ALB routed to the right TG, but TLS handshake happens at ALB. If ALB terminates with wrong cert, upstream nginx never sees client cert.

sunil: Right - ALB TLS listener chooses cert based on ClientHello.sni. If SNI missing or truncated ALB falls back to default cert. We saw a class of NAT boxes that strip or corrupt SNI on re-used connections. Also session affinity (cookie) could be sticky to a node that has a different expected cert mapping.

nate: Reproducer I used: 
```
openssl s_client -connect edge.example.com:443 -servername app-cust.example.com -showcerts
```
Result: subject CN=default-edge.example.com, not app-cust. So ALB never received SNI or chose fallback.

jordan: Any tcpdump from the failing client? Does ClientHello include SNI?

cami: Captured on node: tcpdump -n -s0 -w /tmp/hello.pcap port 443 and ran tshark -V on ClientHello - SNI is absent for ~30% of failing flows. Packet lengths look like MTU path issues (handshake split).

sunil: That rings a bell — path MTU/fragmentation can split ClientHello and ALB's TLS listener can't reassemble SNI reliably at edge. When ALB can't parse SNI it falls back to default cert. Combined with our per-host certs that live only as non-defaults, clients get wrong cert and mTLS breaks.

sam: Oof. Two mitigations: 1) Add critical customer cert as ALB default for the affected IP ranges (bad for scale), 2) Put an NLB/TCP pass-through in front of the cluster so ingress (nginx) sees the full ClientHello including SNI and can handle mTLS itself. Option 2 preserves end-to-end TLS and client cert validation.

nate: Short-term: can we route affected ASNs/ips to a fallback LB with the wildcard cert so they at least get the wildcard and proceed? Long-term I prefer NLB passthrough for mTLS customers.

cami: I ran a small test: created an NLB TCP listener (443) -> target group that forwards raw TCP to nginx. With curl --resolve to force host, the ingress got the full ClientHello and mTLS succeeded. So pass-through fixes it.

infra-bot: deploy:infra: rolling update started for lb/fallback-nlb at 2026-03-18T07:15:00Z by sam

jordan: Risks for NLB route: we lose ALB WAF + HTTP routing features. Need separate path for path-based routing traffic. We'll need to ensure healthchecks and target group configs align and update DNS/route53 weighted records for gradual cutover.

sam: Plan: 1) Nate to scope set of impacted prefixes and open support ticket to AWS for ALB SNI reassembly (low chance), 2) Cami to spin up NLB passthrough for affected customers and wire a canary (weighted DNS 10% -> 100%), 3) I'll add an ingress flag to accept passthrough traffic on dedicated ports and enable proxy_protocol v2 to preserve client info.

nate: I'll also add an infra-monitoring alert for sudden spike in 'SNI absent' ClientHello counts and a dashboard tile.

sunil: TL;DR: cause = fragmented/missing SNI -> ALB default cert -> mTLS client cert check fails. Short-term fallback NLB with wildcard/default cert or route to ingress passthrough. Long-term: review cert placement and consider end-to-end TLS for mTLS customers. :thumbsup:

sam: I'll open PRs for DNS routing + terraform for the NLB canary. Assigning follow-ups in the ticket. Thanks all. :eyes:
